summary: Anomaly detection alerts link to stale model-version traces after nightly compaction
description:
Issue summary:
Anomaly-detection alerts for Glyph Health’s production routes fired between 2026-03-10T02:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:15Z. When support engineers or customers click the 'View root cause traces' link in the Console alert card, the trace list contains spans referencing a stale model version tag (model_version: v2025-11-02) instead of the expected v2026-02-28. This made it appear that the anomaly was caused by an older model, delaying triage.

Impact:
- Glyph Health saw 12 anomaly alerts for sudden latency/embedding drift on several production routes.
- Console root-cause links pointed to traces whose metadata indicated older model versions and older client ids, hindering investigation.
- No inference correctness/regression at model serving layer was identified; this is an observability/indexing mismatch causing confusion and wasted triage time.

Environment:
prod / us-east (Glyph Health dedicated pool). Tracing and alerting pipelines: trace-indexer v2.4.1, metadata-enricher v1.7. Nightly compaction: events-compact-v2 job.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided + reproduced by Support):
1) In Console, open Glyph Health -> Alerts -> Anomaly detection.
2) Click an anomaly card from 2026-03-10 02:20Z window.
3) Click 'View root cause traces' on the card.
4) Inspect trace metadata header (model_version, model_id, request_time).
Expected: trace metadata shows model_version matching the route pin (v2026-02-28).
Observed: trace metadata shows model_version v2025-11-02 for the majority (~70%) of traces returned.

Logs / snippets:
- trace-indexer logs (2026-03-10T02:00Z - 03:30Z): "WARN: out-of-order write to metadata.index for trace_id=trc_8ba, metadata_ts=2025-11-02T12:20:04Z"
- events-compact-v2 logs: "INFO: compacted 3.2M events into index shard us-east-3 (start=2026-03-10T01:58Z, duration=430s)"
- metadata-enricher: "ERROR: enrichment queue lag spike (lag=320s) at 2026-03-10T02:05Z; retrying"

Investigation notes (SRE/Eng):
- Hypothesis: concurrent execution of events-compact-v2 and a backlog/retry from metadata-enricher caused older metadata updates to be written after newer trace events had already been indexed, resulting in index-time skew. The trace search API prefers the latest metadata write for a trace_id, and due to race during compaction we ended up with stale model_version values winning the merge.
- We reproduced locally by running a compaction simulation while re-applying archived metadata writes; the trace search returned the older model_version in similar conditions.
- Affected query path: console -> alert-rollup-service -> trace-search (which reads metadata via metadata-join). The metadata-join logic uses a last-write-wins heuristic without strong causality checks.
- Related code areas: trace-indexer merge routine (src/index/merge.go), metadata-enricher ordering batch (src/enrich/orderer.py).

Temporary mitigation implemented (2026-03-10 09:40Z):
- Blocked events-compact-v2 for remaining us-east compaction window until a safe-replay patch is deployed.
- Rolled out a conservative fallback in trace-search: when model_version timestamp is older than trace span timestamp by >24h, the UI will show "model metadata may be out of date" banner and provide raw span link. This reduces misattribution while we fix merge logic.

Resolution plan / next steps:
1) Short-term (24-72h): implement a server-side guard in trace-indexer that prefers metadata whose write_ts >= span_ts (PR #4218). Deploy staged canary to us-east-1.
2) Mid-term (1-2 weeks): update metadata-enricher to persist causal write ordering (introduce sequence numbers) and make compaction idempotent with rewrite-safe merging.
3) Postmortem and runbook updates: document compaction/enrichment interaction and add a pre-compact check for pending enrichment queue depth.

Comments:
- [Support | 2026-03-10T03:45Z] Jordan (Support): "Customer reported root-cause links pointing to older model metadata. Collected traces and forwarded to SRE with trace IDs and timeline."
- [Customer | 2026-03-10T04:10Z] Maya R. (Glyph Health): "Thanks — once root-cause links pointed to the right model version we could rule out model regression. Appreciate the quick banner workaround."
- [SRE | 2026-03-10T08:20Z] Priya Singh: "Reproduced locally and confirmed compaction + enrichment backlog races produce stale metadata in index. Drafting patch to prefer metadata with write_ts >= span_ts."
- [Eng | 2026-03-11T11:05Z] Diego Marquez: "PR #4218 opened: add timestamp sanity check and opt-in canary. Scheduling canary deploy to us-east-1 at 2026-03-12T02:00Z."

Notes for CS handoff to Customer Success:
- Customer is dedicated with active SLA. They logged this as confusing (not service outage). Recommend follow-up call to explain safeguards and timeline for mid-term fix.

Tags for internal follow-up: runbook update, compaction-safety, enrichment-queue-monitoring, UI-banners
